title: Completion of a weakly cartesian spectral extension as an isometric product
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value and let $H=\widehat F$ be its metric completion [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion], the complete field of equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences with its extended absolute value. Let $E/F$ be a finite field extension, of dimension $n\ge1$, and let $s=s_{E/F}$ be its minimal-polynomial spectral norm [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. Suppose there are an $F$-basis $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ of $E$ and real constants $c,C>0$ with $$c\max_i|a_i|\le s\left(\sum_i a_iw_i\right)\le C\max_i|a_i|\qquad(a_i\in F).$$ Let $\widehat E$ be the metric completion of the normed vector space $(E,s)$: equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences for $s(x-y)$, with the extended norm $\widehat s([(x_m)])=\lim_m s(x_m)$. Termwise multiplication and scalar multiplication by Cauchy sequences from $F$ make $\widehat E$ a commutative $H$-algebra; the canonical map $E\to\widehat E$ is an isometric $F$-algebra embedding with dense image, and $\dim_H\widehat E=n$. There exist $r\ge1$ finite field extensions $L_1,\ldots,L_r$ of $H$ and an $H$-algebra isomorphism $$\theta:\widehat E\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{j=1}^rL_j$$ such that $$\widehat s(z)=\max_{1\le j\le r}s_{L_j/H}(\theta(z)_j)\qquad(z\in\widehat E),\qquad\sum_j[L_j:H]=n.$$ No stability of $F$ or $H$, and no separability of $E/F$, is assumed.

proof.text: Write $N([(x_m)])=\lim_m s(x_m)$. The norm axioms of [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] give $|s(x)-s(y)|\le s(x-y)$, so this limit exists and is unchanged by an equivalent Cauchy sequence. It vanishes exactly on the zero class: $N([(x_m)])=0$ means $s(x_m)\to0$. Sums, negatives and products of representatives define operations on $A=\widehat E$. For products, Cauchy sequences have bounded norms, and $$s(x_my_m-x_ky_k)\le\max(s(x_m)s(y_m-y_k),s(y_k)s(x_m-x_k)).$$ This tends to zero; the same estimate with equivalent representatives proves independence. All commutative ring identities hold termwise. Constant sequences preserve $1$, and their norm is $s(x)$, so $E\to A$ is an injective isometric algebra map. Its image is dense since the constants $x_m$ converge to $[(x_m)]$. Taking limits gives the ultrametric inequality, submultiplicativity and $N(1)=1$.

proof.text: The field $H=\widehat F$ is complete and contains $F$ isometrically by [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. Its absolute value remains nontrivial and ultrametric by restriction and passage to limits. For $h=[(a_m)]\in H$ and $z=[(x_m)]\in A$, define $hz=[(a_mx_m)]$. The estimate in step 1 and scalar homogeneity of $s$ prove that this is well-defined and $N(hz)=|h|N(z)$. The scalar and algebra laws hold termwise. Now write $x_m=\sum_i a_{im}w_i$. The lower bound $c\max_i|a_{im}-a_{ik}|\le s(x_m-x_k)$ shows each coordinate sequence is Cauchy. The upper bound shows conversely that coordinatewise Cauchy sequences give an $s$-Cauchy sequence, and that two such sequences are equivalent exactly when all coordinate differences tend to zero. Thus $$A\longrightarrow H^n,\quad [(x_m)]\longmapsto ([(a_{im})])_i$$ is a bijection, linear for the scalar action just constructed. Surjectivity follows by choosing representatives for the finitely many coordinates. Consequently $\dim_H A=n$, with basis the constant classes of $w_i$. The inequalities extend to $H^n$ by limits, so this model is complete as well: an $N$-Cauchy sequence has Cauchy coordinates, whose limits converge for $N$ by the upper bound.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-algebraic-spectral-norm-powers], $s(x^m)=s(x)^m$ for every $x\in E$ and $m\ge1$. For $z=[(x_k)]$, the product construction in step 1 gives $z^m=[(x_k^m)]$, hence $$N(z^m)=\lim_k s(x_k^m)=\lim_k s(x_k)^m=N(z)^m.$$ If $z^m=0$, this implies $N(z)^m=0$ and therefore $z=0$. Thus $A$ is reduced. It is Artinian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], applied to the $H$-algebra of dimension $n$ from step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] to obtain its canonical product of residue fields $L_j=A/\mathfrak m_j$. Give each $L_j$ the $H$-structure induced by $H\to A\to L_j$; the product isomorphism $\theta$ is then $H$-linear and multiplicative. Each quotient is spanned over $H$ by the images of the $n$ basis vectors, so each $L_j/H$ is finite. There is at least one factor: otherwise $A$ would be the zero ring, contrary to $N(1)=1$. Finally a basis in each product slot gives a basis of the product, proving $\sum_j[L_j:H]=\dim_H A=n$.

proof.text: Let $e_j\in A$ be the preimage under $\theta$ of $1$ in slot $j$ and $0$ elsewhere. It is a nonzero idempotent. Step 3 gives $N(e_j)^2=N(e_j^2)=N(e_j)$, and definiteness implies $N(e_j)=1$. For $b\in L_j$, let $\iota_j(b)$ be its image in that single slot, pulled back to $A$, and set $N_j(b)=N(\iota_j(b))$. This injection is additive, multiplicative and $H$-linear, with $\iota_j(1)=e_j$. Thus $N_j$ is definite, ultrametric, submultiplicative, homogeneous over $H$, normalized at $1$, and power-multiplicative, by steps 1–3. The field $H$ is complete, nontrivially valued and ultrametric by step 2, and $L_j/H$ is algebraic since it is finite. The hypotheses of [lem-trf-power-multiplicative-algebra-norm-unique] therefore hold, giving $N_j(b)=s_{L_j/H}(b)$ for all $b$.

proof.text: For $z\in A$, one has $z=\sum_j ze_j$ and $ze_j=\iota_j(\theta(z)_j)$. The ultrametric inequality gives $N(z)\le\max_j N(ze_j)$. Conversely submultiplicativity and $N(e_j)=1$ give $N(ze_j)\le N(z)$ for every $j$. Combining these two inequalities and step 4 proves $$\widehat s(z)=N(z)=\max_j N_j(\theta(z)_j)=\max_j s_{L_j/H}(\theta(z)_j).$$ This proves the required isometry together with the dimension and dense-embedding assertions already established. No step imposed separability or stability.
